key_insight: ACE and its graph generalization GRACE provide a common basis for comparing interatomic potentials, revealing that much architectural diversity comes from nonlinear parameterization, layer coupling and optimization.
engineering_relevance: Choosing MLIPs along an accuracy–speed Pareto front can reduce atomistic simulation costs while preserving the accuracy needed for materials discovery.
method: Represent classical potentials and modern MLIPs in a canonical expansion of single-particle functions.
Analyze linear scaling with system size and, at fixed tensor-decomposition rank, model complexity.
Compare accuracy and computational cost across model depths and basis truncations.
evidence_signal: On Matbench Discovery, three- to five-layer models approach deeper-model accuracy, while Pareto-front truncations of one basis span more than two orders of magnitude in cost.
watch_item: Training data ultimately determine MLIP quality, so efficient architecture alone does not ensure reliable predictions.
